assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general operation. Ligand design (bulky phosphines, biaryl phosphines) is a clear conceptual advance and its use is visible in countless medicinal and process syntheses.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination with the decisive ligand and mechanistic work; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor but the broadly useful catalytic method is theirs. Two laureates is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation, industrial adoption at scale and textbook status. Recognition is arguably overdue, and the cross-coupling area was already honored in 2010, which may be argued as partial overlap.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize
Credit for Kosugi's precursor chemistry is excluded from my proposed laureates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization changes the logic of retrosynthesis by treating C-H bonds as functional handles. Directing-group, ligand-accelerated and template-controlled approaches allow site-selective transformations used in late-stage functionalization and total synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand and template control of selectivity, enantioselective C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II)/Pd(IV) catalysis, fluorination) and Hartwig (borylation, iridium catalysis) made distinct decisive contributions. Credit is spread, so a three-way split is plausible but Yu is clearly central.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and widely adopted, though the general selectivity problem is not fully solved and industrial use is less routine than for cross-coupling. Hartwig also appears under B011, so overlap in recipients may matter.
uncertainties: Breadth of credit across many groups including Daugulis and Smith
Real-world adoption still growing versus established cross-coupling

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions (decarboxylative, dual catalysis with Ni) not accessible by thermal two-electron chemistry. A distinct and broadly used toolbox.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational 2008-2009 organic photoredox reports; Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi are also strong. MacMillan is already a 2021 laureate, which complicates a fair configuration; a prize for Yoon and Stephenson alone would be defensible but contentious.
assessment.maturity: Mature in use across pharma and academia with extensive independent confirmation, and the field is still evolving. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: MacMillan already awarded in 2021, and dual-catalysis credit versus earlier Fukuzumi and Konig work
Priority among many contributors is disputed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermolecular oxidative addition of unreactive alkane C-H bonds to iridium was a landmark that showed saturated hydrocarbons can be activated at a metal center. It is a conceptual foundation for later catalytic C-H functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Bergman is credited alone, but William Graham's parallel iridium work at the same time is a recognized co-discovery not in the supplied names; the credited name list limits a fair configuration. A single-laureate prize is possible but may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Stoichiometric discovery dating to 1982 with abundant confirmation; practical catalytic alkane functionalization remains limited, so impact is largely conceptual. Recognition is long overdue if at all.
uncertainties: Parallel discovery by Graham is not among the credited names
Limited direct synthetic application of the original stoichiometric chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts. N-heterocyclic carbenes now underpin metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling ligands and organocatalysis, and a new view of main-group bonding.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's stable phosphinocarbene (1988) and Arduengo's crystalline NHC (1991) are the decisive discoveries; Nolan and Rovis shaped catalytic applications but the foundational isolation belongs to the first two.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of confirmation and broad application in industry and academia. Mature and timely, with a clear conceptual novelty in molecule-making.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of Bertrand's carbene versus Arduengo's NHC
Application credit (Nolan, Rovis, Bode) is spread

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered acid-base pairs activate H2 and small molecules without metals, enabling metal-free hydrogenation. It is a surprising and easily taught concept that opened a new area of main-group reactivity.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 reversible H2 activation and Erker's related work are the central contributions; the pair is a natural configuration, and Stephan is the clearer originator.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely extended, but practical synthetic impact (substrate scope, catalyst loading) is still modest compared with established catalysis; arguably somewhat early.
uncertainties: Limited practical adoption in synthesis so far
Priority overlap with earlier Power and others on related reactivity

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides to build proteins by total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis. It is a genuine chemical solution to making large, defined biomolecules and is widely used.
assessment.attribution: Dawson and Kent introduced NCL in 1994 and Muir developed expressed protein ligation, extending it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are also notable, so a three-way recognition is plausible but leaves some credit unassigned.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use with strong independent confirmation. Mature; routine total synthesis of proteins is still limited to specialist laboratories.
uncertainties: Extent of real-world usage outside specialist groups
Credit among Kent, Dawson, Danishefsky and Muir

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave chemists general control over radical polymerization, enabling defined architectures and block copolymers with simple catalysts, and is used in materials and industry.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and the Sawamoto group reported the Ru- and Cu-mediated variants concurrently in 1995; Wang is co-author with Matyjaszewski. Credit between the two lines is balanced but a three-person split is possible.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely applied, with independent confirmation. Competing controlled-radical methods such as RAFT and nitroxide-mediated polymerization limit uniqueness of the prize case.
uncertainties: Overlap with RAFT as a competing method of comparable impact
Allocation between Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto lines
